ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle AED$, with point D on side BC. If $\angle EAB = 50^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ADE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle AED$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAC = \angle EAD$,\\
$\therefore \angle EAB + \angle BAD = \angle DAC + \angle BAD$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAC = \angle EAB = 50^\circ$,\\
$\because AD = AC$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC = \angle C = \angle ADE = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - \angle DAC) = \boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, B, D, C are on the same base, and D is between B and C; A is above the base and slightly to the right, E is in the upper left. The sides AB, AC, BC of triangle ABC are drawn in the figure, and the sides AE, AD, DE of triangle AED are also drawn. The target angle ∠ADE is the angle at point D formed by DA and DE, and this angle is also marked near D in the figure. Then reason: It is known that △ABC ≅ △AED, and according to the written order of congruence, the corresponding vertices are A↔A, B↔E, C↔D. Therefore ∠BAC = ∠EAD, and AC = AD. It can be seen from the figure that ray AD is located in the relevant interior position of ∠BAC and ∠EAD, so the angles can be decomposed as: ∠BAC = ∠BAD + ∠DAC, ∠EAD = ∠EAB + ∠BAD. Because ∠BAC = ∠EAD, ∠BAD + ∠DAC = ∠EAB + ∠BAD. Eliminating the common ∠BAD gives ∠DAC = ∠EAB = 50°. Also because AC = AD, △ACD is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠ADC and ∠ACD are equal. Thus each base angle is (180° - 50°)/2 = 65°. By the congruence correspondence, ∠ADE corresponds to angle C in △ABC, and is also equal to this base angle, so ∠ADE = 65°.
